sections.text: Chemical
Technical Procedure

Title
 Volatile and Fixed Matter in Sludge.
Procedure
Using Standard Method 14th Edition, 1976, p.94
Introduction

Volatile and fixed solids 
in sludge are determined by evaporating a weighted sample on a steam bath. 
Unlike 
total solid matter in wastewater which is expressed in mg/L solids in sludge are 
expressed in terms of percent.

This document initiated by Chem. Mahasen Abd EL-Fattah reviewed by Hoda Hasaneen by 
quality control Chemist Saad Sadeek Hasanen, 
and accepted by eng. Fathy Mahmoud Ragab and approved by Eng: Awad M Fatthy Head Sector of Talkha Power Station.

This document is accepted by eng. Samir 
Abd El Gilil EDEPC MPIS coordinator, and certified by accountant; Mahmoud 
Mohamed Soliman; EDEPC admin and financial inspection, quality control General 
Director and supervisor of inspection and quality control head sector.
Significance

Determination of total 
suspended solids in water by filtration of a well mixed sample. The residue is 
ignited at 550C 50C to a constant weight. Results are reported as milligrams of 
total nonfilterable residue per liter of sample. The determination is useful in 
control of wastewater treatment plant operation because it offers a rough 
approximation of the amount of organic matter present in the solid fraction of 
wastewater, activated sludge, and industrial wastes.
Definitions

Fixed solids is the term applied to the residue of total, suspended, or 
dissolved solids after heating to dryness for a specific time at a specified 
temperature. The weight loss on ignition is called volatile solids.
Safety Precautions

Store 
sample in resistant-glass or plastic bottles.

Begin analysis as soon as possible because it's 
impractical to be preserved the sample.

If necessary refrigerate sample at 4C up to time of 
analysis to minimize microbiological decomposition of solids.
Bring samples to room temperature before analysis.

The temperature at which the residue is dried has an important bearing on 
results.
Each sample require close attention to desiccation after drying.
Some evaporation residues readily absorb moisture; rapid weighing is essential.

The glass fiber disk will fuse at slightly above
550C; therefore, it's important not to 
exceed this temperature when the crucible is ignited.

sections.text:
Tools and 
Equipment
Apparatus

a) Evaporating dishes - 
 Dishes of 100 ml capacity made of
porcelain, 90-mm diam.

b) Muffle furnace- For operation at 550oC 
 50oC,

c) Desiccator- 
 Provided with a desiccant containing a color 
 indicator of moisture concentration,

d) Analytical balance- 
 200 g capacity, capable of weighing to 0.1 mg,

e) Drying oven- 
 For operation at 103 -105oC and
f) Steam bath.
Work to be Carried out

Place 
an adequately-sized evaporating dish in a drying oven 
 at 103 -105oC for 15 or 20 min. after 
cleaning, then air-cool slightly and put the dish in a desiccator for complete cooling 
before weighing. Weight dish and record as W1

Pour 
a portion of the well-mixed sample ( 25 to 50 ml ) into the dish, then weight 
sample and dish together. Record as W2

Place 
dish on a steam bath and evaporate to dryness then put the dish in drying oven 
for 1h at 
103C,
cool in a desiccator, and weight. 
Record the weight as W3

After 
weighing the dish and dry solids, compute the percent total solids ( Equation1 ).

Place 
dish from step 4 in muffle furnace at 550C until sample is burned completely. Length of time for complete burning depends on size of sample.

Cool 
slightly, then put dish in desiccator for complete cooling before weighing. Weight the dish and record 
as W4 
. The loss of weight ( W3-W4 ) 
is the volatile matter. The percent volatile matter then may be computed ( 
Equation 2 ).

Weight of volatile solids (W3-W4)

Percent Volatile Matter = ----------------------------------

Precision

Repeat 
 cycle of igniting, cooling, desicating, and weighing until a constant weight 
 is obtained or until weight change is less than 4% or 0.5 mg, whichever is 
 less. Duplicate determinations should agree within 5% of their average.
